bars.title: Earned speed is kept
bars.statement: After leaving the cap at 2× cruise by ANY means (rope release, shove, well fling, bounce), speed 10 s later is ≥ 99 % of the exit speed with hands off, and ≥ 99 % with forward held. Only the brake spends it.
bars.target: ≥ 99 % of exit speed 10 s later, hands off and forward held

values.label: release speed kept 5 s after letting go, hands off (worst of 1 run(s))
speed kept 10 s after a 2x cruise exit, hands off
speed kept 10 s after a 2x cruise exit, forward held

bars.notes: only the 5 s release-retention clause (≥ 95 %) was measured; that sentence belongs to the rope-release scenario, and the value row is kept for the receipt. B1's own clauses — ≥ 99 % of exit speed 10 s later, hands off and with forward held — are kernel-level (test/flightV3.spec.mjs §12c) and are not benched headlessly, so this bar cannot read met from this bench. exit 389.99810791015625 WU/s from a physics impulse; cruise 194.99905395507812 WU/s exit 389.99810791015625 WU/s from a physics impulse; cruise 194.99905395507812 WU/s

bars.title: The rope is a rope
bars.statement: Swinging at 1.5× cruise on a 100 WU line around a heavy anchor stretches the line < 10 % and does not break; releasing at the tangent keeps ≥ 95 % of tangential speed 5 s later.
bars.target: stretch < 10 %; release keeps ≥ 95 % of tangential speed at 5 s

values.label: peak line stretch (worst of 1 run(s))
tangential speed kept 5 s after release (worst of 1 run(s))

bars.notes: the verb scenario swings at cruise (195 WU/s) on an 80 WU line, not the contract's 1.5× cruise on a 100 WU line around a heavy anchor. Line break is not instrumented (the bench detaches the tether by design at release).

bars.statement: The dedicated shove weapon changes a light hostile's velocity by ≥ 30 % of its cruise per hit. The starter gun changes it by ≥ 5 % per hit. A light hostile already at cruise gets faster when shoved along its motion.

starter gun delta-V, fraction of light-hostile cruise
light hostile at cruise shoved ALONG its motion gets faster (speed after / speed before)

bars.notes: the verdict applies the contract's 0.30 threshold; the bench-internal barB4Met boolean uses a looser 0.15 and is ignored here. The starter-gun ≥ 5 % clause and the faster-along-its-motion clause are unbenched.

bars.title: Shove displacement

bars.target: ≥ 1 screen depth off the original line 2 s after the hit

values.label: displacement 2 s after the shove, screen depths (worst of 1 run(s))
victim has not fired within 2 s of the shove-weapon hit

bars.title: Hitstun law is universal
bars.statement: Helm-loss duration is one function of (ΔV ÷ cruise) and (attacker mass ÷ victim mass) for guns, throws, flings and collisions alike; lights at ≥ 30 % ΔV lose the helm ≥ 1 s; heavies at gun-scale ΔV never do. NPCs recover with real thruster torque, never a hidden gyro.
bars.target: one universal curve; lights ≥ 30 % ΔV stunned ≥ 1 s; heavies at gun-scale ΔV never

values.label: shove helm-loss duration, scenario constant (measured at only 13 % of cruise, below the ≥ 30 % ΔV regime)
terrain slam strips the helm (1 run(s))
light hull loses the helm >= 1 s at measured k >= 0.30 - gun
light hull loses the helm >= 1 s at measured k >= 0.30 - rope_throw
light hull loses the helm >= 1 s at measured k >= 0.30 - well_fling
light hull loses the helm >= 1 s at measured k >= 0.30 - collision
heavy hull at gun-scale delta-V never loses the helm (measured k <= 0.06, all sources)
one law: relative spread of helm-loss across the four sources at matched k (light hull, k ~ 0.30)
helm-loss is monotone non-decreasing in k (light hull, gun source)

bars.notes: measured below the ≥ 30 % ΔV regime; helm duration is the scenario constant, not a measured curve, and the ≥ 1 s helm clause cannot be evaluated from it. the universal-curve sweep (one helm-loss function of ΔV ÷ cruise and attacker ÷ victim mass across guns, throws, flings and collisions) is unbenched. gun 0.4833s, rope_throw 4.1333s, well_fling 0s, collision 1.5s

bars.title: The player is never knocked around
bars.statement: In ten minutes of ordinary flight (no rope, no fields, no deliberate ram), contact changes the player's velocity ≤ 2 times per minute and never by more than 10 % of cruise in one event, never changes the player's heading, and never produces visible jitter; a deliberate big event (a slam the player chose, a well the player flew into) may, and it must be legible.
bars.target: ≤ 2 contact knocks per minute; largest ≤ 10 % of cruise; zero heading changes; no visible jitter

values.label: contact knocks per minute on the player, verbs feel.knock_budget (worst of 1 run(s))
largest single knock, fraction of cruise, verbs feel.knock_budget (worst of 1 run(s))
knock events that changed the player's heading (worst of 1 run(s); contract target zero)

bars.notes: the visible-jitter clause and the legible-deliberate-event clause are unbenched.

bars.title: Impacts answer
bars.statement: Every collision with ΔV ≥ 8 WU/s produces hitstop and camera trauma scaled by exchanged momentum. Collision audio differs by ≥ one octave of pitch and ≥ 12 dB between a scout kissing a rock and a freighter broadsiding a station. A Massline release has a time-domain snap.
bars.target: hitstop + trauma at ΔV ≥ 8 WU/s; audio ≥ 1 octave and ≥ 12 dB apart; release snaps

values.label: collision audio pitch, scout-on-rock vs freighter-on-station
collision audio loudness, same two cases
Massline razor release time-domain snap

bars.notes: hitstop, camera trauma and audio are presentation-layer; the headless bench has no instrument for them. the bar is listed here for completeness; this bench cannot measure it. hard-coded 0 on all nine branches before PQ-139.00
